answer: Agents mint one capacity bond per identity: stake locks for several epochs before any reward vests. A falcon-style random audit pulls onyx digests of recent work graphs; clones that share graphs or timing patterns burn the bond and forfeit pending earnings. Spawning N sockpuppets therefore costs N bonds plus correlated slash risk, so forging identities is linear-cost and negative-EV versus a single walnut-honest account that keeps its stake.
